item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00021","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C02","C04","C08"],"selected_candidate_label":"C02","confidence":0.96,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C02 plausibly supplied a material foundation for the child. The child expressly recounts the housing curtailment instituted the previous summer, and C02 is the directive that imposed that curtailment, including a numerical limit on commencing public-housing construction. Both documents use the same defense-mobilization framework—scarce construction materials, reduced residential construction, preservation of preferences, and calibrated limits on public housing—but the child adapts it to argue that the House's much harsher limitation would frustrate the equitable policy established in C02. C04 has a similar congressional-appropriations appeal and national-security justification, while C08 supplies extensive substantive advocacy for the Housing Act of 1949, but neither matches C02's specific policy machinery and factual continuity.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Last summer, when it became necessary to curtail total home construction in the interest of the defense effort, plans for building low rent public housing were cut back proportionately.","parent_excerpt":"Limit the commencement of construction of public housing to not more than 30,000 dwelling units in the first six months of fiscal year 1951, during which time the public housing program should be thoroughly reexamined in terms of the developing international situation.","explanation":"The child directly describes and evaluates the public-housing curtailment ordered in C02."},{"child_excerpt":"In the January budget, funds were requested for only 75,000 new units in fiscal 1952. This contrasts with the 135,000 units per year authorized by the Housing Act of 1949 and is well in line with the 40 percent over-all reduction which we have been seeking in the pre-Korean volume of new starts.","parent_excerpt":"many materials used in residential and other construction will be required in increasing amounts for national defense purposes... unless positive actions are taken to reduce pressures in residential construction.","explanation":"Both frame reduced housing starts as a measured response to defense-related competition for construction materials."},{"child_excerpt":"In reducing the volume of housing starts, our aim has been to spread the remaining supply equitably among all income groups.","parent_excerpt":"It is my wish that both agencies accomplish a substantial and parallel curtailment of housing credit, but in such a way that the relative preference presently accorded veterans is preserved.","explanation":"Both stress that housing restraint should be coordinated and should preserve equitable or preferred treatment rather than impose a disproportionate burden."}]}
